coaching.headline: Khaimera died eleven times, and the allied side owned the big objectives, from the first Fangtooth to the Shaper.

flags.text: Every later Fangtooth, Prime and the Shaper came under two minutes after a Khaimera death.
Yin last-hit all eight Fangtooth, Prime and Shaper takes; 59964 objective damage led all ten.
Lt. Belica's damage was damn near unfair: 50686 to heroes, the most of all ten, one death.
The shit stretch: Legion and Narbash died on the duo lane, then all three allied outer towers fell.

focus.title: Jungler down, pit next
focus.action: Keep starting Fangtooth or Prime right after each Khaimera death. Before the outer towers fall, Legion and Narbash take duo-lane fights only when Khaimera shows on another lane.

14.6.call: Steel and Khaimera took two duo-lane kills with nothing traded back. With two allies down, the other three defend one tower together, not three.

29.6.call: Yin and Scarlett killed Khaimera and Shinbi at the Prime pit, and Orb Prime and the Shaper went allied next. Clean conversion; repeat the pattern.

35.2.call: Primal Fangtooth first, then The Fey and Shinbi fell at the pit and Drongo on the duo lane before Legion razed the Core.

0503af2c-6844-43bb-bf20-0d97b25097f4: Razed the enemy mid outer, duo outer and the Core, with 15344 objective damage, second of all ten. After each won duo fight, hit the nearest tower first.
Both deaths came before the allied duo outer fell: one to Drongo outside any detected fight, one to Steel in the lost duo-lane fight. Early on, farm with Narbash close.
d50f824c-24da-4247-95e0-667544e5963b: Ran the vision and the healing: 29 wards and 29040 healing, the most of all ten in both, with 58% kill participation. Hold that ward pace in every long game.
Razed the enemy offlane inner and duo inhibitor, and the kill on Drongo opened the duo-lane fight that went allied 3-0. When Drongo is isolated, start the pick again.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Zero deaths, 52183 damage mitigated, the most among allies, and 799 hero damage per minute against an own average of 583. Repeat the zero-death standard next game.
No kill or death credit in four fights after the offlane opened, including the won duo-lane fight. Once the offlane opens, join fights with Swan Song ready.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Three kills on other lanes each preceded a prize: the enemy offlane outer, Primal Fangtooth, the Core. The first duo trip preceded a lost mid inner; call for mid cover.
Razed the enemy mid inner, farmed 10.1 CS per minute against an own average of 8.2, and died once, to Khaimera. Keep farming at that rate between rotations.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Four deaths, the most among allies; two came outside any detected fight, in the enemy jungle, to Drongo and Khaimera. Before invading, wait for a laner to follow.
Farmed 8.9 CS per minute against an own average of 6.9 and healed 19103, second of all ten. Keep clearing between majors at that pace.

matchup: Before minute ten the only duo-lane death was Drongo's, to this carry.
Out-damaged Drongo 31042 to 15475 in hero damage; Drongo finished 2/3/2.
Drongo's Gag Grenade silences; Steel's Shield Slam knocks up and stuns, the top ability to wait out.
build: Deathstalker and Vanquisher are two of three winning-core items; Malady is missing.
Viper cuts physical armor on hero damage and, at full stacks, boosts on-hit and ability damage.
Demolisher came last, so only the closing fight had the extra armor ignore.
eternal: Thraex marks the last hero hit by a basic attack: more damage dealt to the mark, less taken from the mark.
Knell, Lotus and Xyris lead a toss-up in this carry field; Thraex, the most played, ranks well behind.
Savage Strikes with Rallying Roar is the best and most played Thraex pair. Sound keep on minors.
augment: Press the Advantage drops a Rally Point on takedowns that raises own rate of fire and grants allies attack speed.
Scorched Earth clearly leads this carry augment field over Press the Advantage, the most played.
crest: Pacifier's active dashes and empowers the next physical hit, much stronger on low-health targets, recast on hero kills.
Epoch and Witchstalker lead a toss-up in this carry field; Pacifier ranks behind both.
improvement: Lane record into Drongo sits at 53.7%; the field core into Drongo adds Malady and Spear Of Desolation to Deathstalker.
Scorched Earth over Press the Advantage is the field-backed swap: napalm zones from mines and ultimate, losing the ally attack speed.

matchup: Duo lane was against Drongo and Steel; neither allied duo player died before minute ten.
Khaimera scored the duo-lane death in the lost fight; Shinbi scored the late death in the enemy base.
Steel's Shield Bash and Shield Slam both stun; Steel placed 11 wards against 29.
build: Truesilver Bracelet is one of three winning-core items; Forticus and Tainted Totem are missing.
Xenia shields a nearby ally, Enra's Blessing shields an immobilized ally, Vanguardian adds both armors to nearby allies.
Vanguardian came last, so the aura covered only the last three fights.
eternal: Exarch gives healed or shielded targets attack speed and bonus magical damage on basic attacks.
Lotus and Aion lead a toss-up in this support field; Exarch, the most played, trails both.
Preservation with Delayed Fate is the best Exarch pair; the run pair, Preservation with Omnipresent, is the most played.
augment: Percussive Tear makes each Crash Bang Boom! hit shred both armors briefly.
Thonk clearly leads this support augment field over Percussive Tear, the most played.
crest: Sanctification's active shields self and nearby heroes with tenacity while the shield holds; Visionary raises the ward cap.
Reclamation leans ahead of Sanctification in this support field.
improvement: Into Steel, the most played field core pairs Truesilver Bracelet with Crystal Tear and Dynamo: 56.2% over 73 games.
Thonk over Percussive Tear is the field-backed swap: cooldown and mana refunds on Thunk pickups, losing the armor shred.
Delayed Fate over Omnipresent matches the best Exarch pair: ability damage spread over time instead of out-of-combat speed.

matchup: Shinbi was the lane opponent: two kills on Shinbi, zero deaths, and Shinbi finished 2/6/2.
Of 27820 hero damage taken, 18458 was magical, from an enemy team with three magical heroes.
Killed Khaimera twice on the offlane; Khaimera's Cull suppresses in an area.
build: Mutilator and Infernum are two of three winning-core items; The Perforator is missing.
Mistmeadow Buckler blocks part of incoming magical damage and adds magical armor, the right answer to that damage mix.
Rebirth came last and resurrects only after a death; with zero deaths the passive never triggered.
eternal: Knell shreds both armors with Rust stacks on hero hits and returns part of the shred as own armor.
Nihil and Knell lead a toss-up in this offlane field. Sound keep.
Patina with Fracture is the most played Knell pair; Patina with Peal is the best pair.
augment: Volcaic Slam turns empowered Cindara into a delayed eruption that damages and slows enemies.
Field lean favors Volcaic Slam over Scarlet Dawn in this offlane field; keep the pick.
crest: Judgement's active deals area damage and heals on hero hits.
Brutallax and Ortus lead a toss-up in this offlane field; Judgement, the most played, ranks behind both.
improvement: Field core for this offlane pick is Terminus, Vyzar Carapace and Forticus at 60%; none of the three was built.
Brutallax over Judgement stays on the Champion Crest path: a cleanse and tenacity instead of the area heal.
Peal over Fracture matches the best Knell pair: ultimate haste and full Rust on the ultimate, losing bonus damage at max Rust.

matchup: The Fey was the lane opponent: The Fey went 0/3/3 yet razed both allied mid towers that fell.
The Fey's Fly Trap pulls and stuns; the only death came to Khaimera on the mid lane in the allied half.
build: Combustion, Noxia and Wraith Leggings are the full winning core.
Caustica ignores part of magical armor; Spellbreaker adds magical armor and a spell shield that blocks the next ability.
Spellbreaker came last, so only the closing fight had the spell shield.
eternal: Lotus grants a random small stat on a timer and on every takedown.
Lotus leans ahead of Xyris in this mid field. Sound keep.
Flawless with Fragrance trails Early Bloom with Immaculate, the best and most played Lotus pair.
augment: Combat Veteran adds movement speed and passive experience that grows with hero level.
Combat Veteran clearly leads this mid augment field. Sound keep.
crest: Soulbearer's active gives a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed.
Soulbearer leans ahead of Epoch, the most played, in this mid field. Sound keep.
improvement: Built every item of both field cores, the general one at 57.9% and the core into The Fey; no change proven.
Early Bloom with Immaculate over Flawless with Fragrance is the field pair: an extra level and high-health damage reduction, losing ally healing.

matchup: Khaimera was the jungle opponent and finished 4/11/1, five of those deaths to this jungler, first blood included.
Khaimera's two kills on this jungler came in the enemy jungle and on the mid lane; Cull suppresses in an area.
Enemy damage leaned magical: 15349 of 25620 hero damage taken.
build: Sky Splitter and Tainted Rounds are two of three winning-core items; Storm Breaker is missing.
Tainted Rounds cuts the target's healing on basic attacks, trimming Khaimera's E heal and Marrow healing.
No item or crest adds armor of either type.
eternal: Marrow converts hero damage into healing, scaling up as health drops; Blood Bank adds lifesteal from stored hero damage.
Marrow has too few games to lead this jungle field; Weald leans first.
Blood Bank with Roses is the best Marrow pair. Sound keep on minors.
augment: Storm of Salvation extends Windburn and adds healing on hit while Windburn lasts.
Energy Transfer leans ahead of Storm of Salvation, the most played, in this jungle field.
crest: Liberator's active removes all debuffs and grants a brief shield.
Pacifier leans ahead of Eviscerator and Liberator, the most played, in this jungle field.
improvement: Physical armor was the unmet need into Khaimera, a 52.3% matchup for Khaimera; no item answered.
Storm Breaker completes the field core into Khaimera, 64.8% over 54 games, beside the owned Sky Splitter and Tainted Rounds.
Energy Transfer over Storm of Salvation is the field lean: speed and a shield on deflected projectiles, losing on-hit healing.

threats: Heal-stacking: Steel. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Shinbi. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Narbash) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Saturation Charge mines to slow, Frag Order to launch enemies, Orbital Sanction to track them, Rally Point to knock back divers and heal allies.
ourKits.winCondition: Hold an area with Orbital Sanction and mines while Rally Point keeps his team healthy and his rifle on infinite ammo.
ourKits.passive: Ballistic Calibration turns bonus attack speed into ability haste and unlocks ability upgrades at item stat thresholds.
ourKits.playWith: Frontliners who fight inside Rally Point's heal and hold enemies in the Orbital beam.
ourKits.playAgainst: Stun him while he cooks Frag Order to make him drop it. Bait Rally Point's knockback before engaging, trade when he reloads, and buy anti-heal against Rally Point's heal and armor against his physical damage.

ourKits.combo: Thunk to knock back and stun, March! to boost his current Song aura for the team, then channel Crash Bang Boom! to stack slows into a Mesmerize and finish with a knock up and stun.
ourKits.winCondition: Start fights with Thunk and keep the team moving or healing with Song of My People and March!, then lock a group with his ult.
ourKits.passive: Mosh Pit: he gains physical power and both armors for each nearby hero, ally or enemy.
ourKits.playWith: A brawling team that rides his speed or healing aura into fights and follows up on his ult.
ourKits.playAgainst: Sidestep the small Thunk area, and walk out of Crash Bang Boom! early since he slows himself while channeling and it only Mesmerizes at max stacks. Spread out so Mosh Pit gives him fewer stacks.

ourKits.combo: First Intent dash in for a shield, Ashen Vow outer edge to slow and empower Cindara, Swan Song to restrain the target and set her blade Ablaze, then Minueta stabs to execute.
ourKits.winCondition: Land Swan Song on a key target to restrain them and spend the Ablaze window with longer range and more power, finishing with Minueta.
ourKits.passive: Last Light: she uses Energy instead of Mana, restores Energy on takedowns, and turns bonus mana into physical power.
ourKits.playWith: Engage or CC teammates who group enemies for Ashen Vow and help her reach the restrained target.
ourKits.playAgainst: Ashen Vow has a short channel and its slow is on the outer edge, so step inside or away. She is Unstoppable during Swan Song, so save CC for after it; fight her after First Intent's shield is spent. Armor answers her physical damage.

ourKits.combo: Void Drone for vision and mana drain, Seismic Assault to knock up and stun, Void Bomb, then Neural Disruptor to silence and finish.
ourKits.winCondition: Drain mana with Void Drone and land Seismic Assault, then burst with Neural Disruptor's missing-mana damage.
ourKits.passive: Innovation upgrades each ability at max rank and grants ability haste.
ourKits.playWith: Follow-up damage during Seismic Assault's knockup and stun.
ourKits.playAgainst: Seismic Assault erupts after a short delay, so sidestep the line. Avoid casting near Void Drone since it zaps and drains mana, and dive her after Seismic Assault is used; magical armor helps.

ourKits.combo: Lash Kick in for the slow → Windburn for range and cleave → third-hit max-health damage and heal → Backlash to push away, Quelling Gale to stop projectiles
ourKits.winCondition: stick with Lash Kick, ramp Rising Storm attack speed and out-trade with Windburn's healing third hits
ourKits.passive: Rising Storm stacks from basics and Lash Kick grant attack speed
ourKits.playWith: a team that lets her side-lane and pick off isolated targets
ourKits.playAgainst: Backlash reflects projectiles and Quelling Gale halts them, so use melee or ground effects while they are up; fight after Lash Kick is used, and buy anti-heal against Windburn

enemyKits.combo: Old Rusty slows on the way out and back, Gag Grenade silences, Rad Rounds stacks Irradiate on basics, then Shrapnel Cannon shreds armor and erupts Irradiate
enemyKits.winCondition: kite from range, stack Wastelander bleed and Rad Rounds, and use Shrapnel Cannon to shred or escape
enemyKits.passive: critical strikes and ability hits apply a max-health bleed
enemyKits.playWith: peel and frontline so he can free-fire
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Gag Grenade's silence; Shrapnel Cannon cast in the air launches him away and is briefly unstoppable, so engage after it is used; armor blunts his physical damage

enemyKits.combo: Rushing Beat dashes through the target → Line Tempo wolf → Circle Rhythm for shield and speed → All-Kill! once Track is maxed
enemyKits.winCondition: hit heroes with abilities to max Track, then cast All-Kill! to drop a wolf pack on every hero she recently damaged
enemyKits.passive: Biting Melody adds magical damage on-hit; every few seconds an empowered basic applies Track and restores mana
enemyKits.playWith: teammates who engage or slow so she can dash in and land every ability for Track
enemyKits.playAgainst: All-Kill! only works once she has stacked Track, so do not trade abilities with her for free; fight after Rushing Beat charges are spent, burst through Circle Rhythm's shield, and buy magical armor if she gets ahead

enemyKits.combo: Bramble Patch slow → Untamed Growth zone → Harvest Nettles stacks → Fly Trap pull and stun
enemyKits.winCondition: land Fly Trap on several heroes and follow with zone damage
enemyKits.passive: takedowns spawn an Untamed Growth and give her movement speed
enemyKits.playWith: engage that holds enemies near her Fly Trap and Bramble Patch
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has no dash, so dive her once Fly Trap is spent; stay out of Bramble Patch and Untamed Growth zones, and buy magical armor

enemyKits.combo: Bull Rush in unstoppable to knock back → Shield Bash stun → Shield Slam knockup and stun, Force Shield to block projectiles
enemyKits.winCondition: engage with Shield Slam or Bull Rush and protect carries with Force Shield's projectile wall
enemyKits.passive: a self-shield that lasts until broken and refreshes when out of damage, plus hybrid armor
enemyKits.playWith: ranged carries he can shield from enemy projectiles, and follow-up damage for his engages
enemyKits.playAgainst: Bull Rush is unstoppable, so do not waste CC into it; walk around Force Shield instead of shooting into it, and fight after Shield Slam is on cooldown

enemyKits.combo: Ambush leap and slow, Unleash for maximum attack speed cleaving basics, Cull to lock the target, Invigorate to cleanse and heal.
enemyKits.winCondition: Stick to one target, build Rage for regen and faster cooldowns, and out-sustain them in long fights.
enemyKits.passive: Ancestral Fury builds Rage on hits, giving health regen and faster cooldowns, plus movement speed at high Rage.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Buy anti-heal to cut Invigorate and Rage regen. Save your CC until after Invigorate is used since it cleanses, and break off for a few seconds so his Rage decays.

ultPlus: Truesilver Bracelet (Reprisal): On casting your Ultimate: Gain a 100 (+18%) Shield for 4s.• While the Shield holds you are CC Immune.• When removed, it explodes dealing Damage equal to 40% of the initial Shield.
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 395 hero damage a minute, more than 87% of Narbash support players this patch (9% of the team's). The damage came from Truesilver Bracelet.
Crash Bang Boom! at top rank: 85s base, about 58.6s by the end (31% shorter) from 45 ability haste: Xenia 10, Void Conduit 10, Enra's Blessing 15, Vanguardian 10.

Truesilver Bracelet (Reprisal): On casting your Ultimate: Gain a 100 (+18%) Shield for 4s.• While the Shield holds you are CC Immune.• When removed, it explodes dealing Damage equal to 40% of the initial Shield.
Narbash dealt 14,210 hero damage, 9% of their team's, with +75 magical power from items.

Truesilver Bracelet (item): On casting your Ultimate: Gain a 100 (+18%) Shield for 4s. While the Shield holds you are CC Immune. When removed, it explodes dealing Damage equal to 40% of the initial Shield.

Sustain: 10% heal and shield power; Truesilver Bracelet: On casting your Ultimate: Gain a 100 (+18%) Shield for 4s. While the Shield holds you are CC Immune. When removed, it explodes dealing Damage equal to 40% of the initial Shield.; Xenia: When within 200u to an Ally Hero: Grant them a 50 (+10%)(+5 per Level) Shield for 4s. Cooldown is per Target.; Enra's Blessing: When within 1000u of an Ally Hero, if they are Immobilized: Grant them a 50 (+30%)(+8%) Shield for 3.5s. Cooldown is per Target.; 29,040 healing recorded.
Toughness: +875 health, +65 physical armor, +100 magical armor, +25% tenacity; took 35,975 damage, mitigated 42,926, died 2 times.

Stack (Kept alive in fights): 4 effects on one trigger: Truesilver Bracelet, Xenia, Enra's Blessing, Vanguardian. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
Countered? 0 of the 2 players Narbash killed built magical armor. We killed Narbash 2 times.
Copy it? Too few Narbash support games with this Eternal or core this patch to say whether it wins elsewhere.

card.lesson: Crash Bang Boom! came back about every 59s instead of 85s by the end (31% shorter). Count it, and take fights while it is down.

evidence: 8/1/9, 50686 hero damage, the most in the game.
Hero damage per minute 1408 vs their Lt. Belica norm 792.

bullets: Exarch gave each ally shielded by Xenia or Enra's Blessing brief attack speed and magical on-hit damage; both shields have per-target cooldowns, Enra's firing only on immobilized allies.
Casting Crash Bang Boom! gave Narbash a Truesilver Bracelet shield and crowd control immunity while the shield held; Preservation enlarged that shield, and Exarch boosted Narbash's basic attacks.
Omnipresent added speed out of combat, getting Narbash to fights sooner, where Mosh Pit grants physical power and both armors for each nearby hero, ally or enemy.
Minueta and Ashen Vow on enemy heroes built Knell's Rust stacks, shredding armor and giving Scarlett part of the shred; Fracture added damage on targets at maximum Rust.
Patina gave Scarlett a shield after a stretch without taking damage, plus movement speed only while that shield held, a cushion before First Intent's own dash shield.
Every basic attack set off Mutilator's max-health damage and built Infernum's Kindling toward an ignite; the ignite dealt more to enemies with more bonus armor.
Belica's ability hits set off Combustion's burst on a cooldown, Wraith Leggings on heroes below 40% Health, and Caustica on heroes above 50% Health with bonus magical armor.
Lotus granted a random small boost, such as damage or ability haste, on a timer and on every takedown; Fragrance raised Belica's magical damage to enemy heroes nearby.
Flawless healed Belica and nearby allies once per cast whenever an ability hit an enemy hero, so Void Bomb and Seismic Assault doubled as small team heals.
Marrow healed Yin for part of hero damage, more at low health; Blood Bank turned recent hero damage into lifesteal, both fed by Sky Splitter and Tainted Rounds.
Roses paid extra gold on takedowns, growing with each earlier takedown up to a cap, and each of Yin's 7 kills briefly strengthened Marrow's healing.
Rising Storm attack speed meant more basic attacks, each setting off Sky Splitter and trimming non-ultimate cooldowns via Ashbringer, once per ability; Windburn's third straight hit healed Yin.
